Mrs. Rubaiyat Hossain, A.A.G, ------ For the petitioner
No one appears ------ For the opposite party
parties:
Government of Bangladesh
Vs.
Kalimuddin Pramanic and others
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain, J: This Rule was issued on an application for revision filed by defendant No. 1 under section 115 (1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) against judgment and decree dated 21.4.1990 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Borgra in Other Class (O.C) Appeal No. 5 of 1985 dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming judgment and decree dated 21.12.1983 passed by the then learned Subordinate Judge, Bogra in O.C. Suit No. 18 of 1977.

2. The plaintiff filed the suit for declaration of title to the suit land and for permanent injunction therein.

3. The case of the plaintiff is that the suit land appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 1 of Mouza Darigachha under P.S. and District-Bogra originally belonged to landlord Bimalendu Roy Bahadur. During C.S. operation, the land was recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 1 in his name. But in the remarks column of the Khatian the suit land was written as “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয” Actually, the local people had no possession in, or prescriptive right over the suit land as such, the recital “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয” in the remarks column of the C.S. Khatian was wrong and illegal.

4. After partition, the then Government of East Pakistan took the khas land of the zamindars in its khas possession and proposed to settle those lands. The plaintiff applied for taking settlement of the suit land from defendant No. 1. On 1.10.1973, the plaintiff was successful in taking settlement of the suit land by executing a registered deed of lease for 10 years from 1374 to 1385 B.S. After that, the plaintiff paid rent to the Government form 1379-1381 B.S. In order to harass the plaintiff, defendant Nos. 3-15 in the name of `Darigacha Samabaya Samity' made a petition for cancelling his lease to defendant No. 2 and as a result, Miscellaneous Case No. 84/13/74-75 was started. The Circle Officer (C.O) (Revenue) enquired into the matter and submitted a report to defendant No. 2. With-out serving any notice upon the plaintiff, a date for hearing of the Miscellaneous Case was fixed for 29.10.1975. As soon as the plaintiff came to know of the date, he went to the office and applied for time and as a result, the date was fixed for hearing on 15.11.1975. Soon afterwards, defendant No. 2 having been influenced by defendant Nos. 3-15 altered the date for hearing from 15.11.1975 to 7.11.1975. Again another notice was issued to the plaintiff restraining him from catching fish from the tank and also restraining him from using its water. Defendant No. 2 did not have the right to cancel the lease as the plaintiff did not violate any terms and conditions of the deed of lease. The plaintiff prayed that the order dated 7.11.1975 cancelling the lease dated 1.10.1975 was illegal, ultra vires and without jurisdiction and that the plaintiffs' title was not affected by the order of cancellation.

5. Defendant No. I filed a written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint. The case of defendant No. 1 is that the suit land is a tank which contains water throughout the year and even there are 6/7 feet water in Chaitra. In collusion with the local Tahsilder, the plaintiff managed to obtain a false report that the suit land was a path land and the local authority having been influenced by the plaintiff submitted a false report. After that, by practicing fraud, the plaintiff managed to obtain an order of lease from the then S.D.O (Sub-divisional Officer) Sadar. As soon as the local people who use the water of the tank for irrigation came to know about the plaintiffs lease, they made a petition for cancellation of the lease to defendant No. 2 who fixed the date on 29.10.75 for hearing. On that date, the plaintiff prayed for time, which was allowed fixing the next date for 15.11.1976. On that very day, the local people applied for early hearing of the case and the date was refixed for 7.11.1975 in place of 15.11.1975. On 7.11.1975, the plaintiff again filed a petition praying for time, which was allowed upto noon of that day. After that, the plaintiff did not appear at the hearing.

6. Considering all the relevant papers, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) rightly cancelled the lease granted to the plaintiff.

7. Defendant Nos. 13 and 14 filed another written statement. Their case is that the land of plot No. 794 is a tank and that plot No. 2446 measuring 7.07 is a part of River Bhadai, used by the local people. Since there is no embankment of the tank, the local people use the water of the tank for irrigation from the time of their forefathers. Accordingly, in the remarks column of the C.S  khatian, the suit land was shown “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয” By practicing fraud upon the local authority and suppressing the rec9rd containing the entry “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয” the plaintiff took settlement of the suit land.

8. Both the parties examined witnesses and adduced documentary evidence in support of their respective cases. The trial Court decreed the suit.

9. Defendant No. 1 appealed against the decree. The appellate Court dismissed the appeal affirming judgment and decree passed by the trial Court.

10. Feeling aggrieved by impugned judgment and decree, defendant No. 1 as the petitioner obtained this Rule from this Court.

11. Mrs. Rubaiyat Hossain, learned Assistant Attorney General appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that according to Rule 22 Register VIII. Chapter-3 of the Government State Manual, 1958, the lands of two plots could not be leased out to the plaintiff and as such, the very lease of the suit land was void ab initio. She further submits that from the report of the Advocate Commissioner, it appears that there were 2 to 21/2 cubit of water in suit plot No. 794 and that suit plot No. 2583 turned into a river during rainy session. She lastly submits that the appellate Court being the final Court of fact miserably failed to write out a judgment as contemplated under Order 41, Rule 31 of the Code.

12. Though the case appeared in the daily cause list on three occasions, none appeared on behalf of plaintiff-opposite party No. 1.

13. Having perused the judgment of the appellate Court, 1 find that the learned. Additional District Judge failed to appreciate the case of the respective parties. The learned Additional District Judge came to a finding that the defendant accepted salami as well as the rent from the plaintiff who performed the terms of the lease and that as such, cancellation of plaintiff's lease was not according to the Rules. The learned Additional District Judge further found that if the settlement was given by the then S.D.O. mistakenly for his incompetence, he should not be retained in service. The learned Additional District Judge, therefore, concluded that the plaintiff acquired a valid title in the suit land on the basis of the lease.

14. The learned Subordinate Judge came to a finding that since the plaintiff did not violate any of the terms of the deed of lease, his lease could not be cancelled. The learned Subordinate Judge found that at the time of settlement of the suit land to the plaintiff, the Circle Officer (Revenue) sent the record with connected papers after enquiry to the S.D.O. for approval with his recommendation and that subsequently, the same Circle Officer submitted another report. The learned Subordinate Judge also found that having been influenced by the local people, the Additional Deputy Commissioner most illegally can-celled the lease given to the plaintiff and that before cancellation, he influenced the Circle Officer for giving such report. While concluding the judgment, the learned Subordinate Judge observed that the Government might resume possession of such land.

15. Having perused C.S. khatian No. 1 of Mouza Darigacha, I find that plot No. 794 was shown as tank and in its remarks column, the tank was shown as “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয” Chapter 111 of the Government State Manual, 1958 gives detailed descriptions of the Register that is to be maintained. According to Rule 22, Register VIII is a register of unoccupied lands and will be maintained in parts:

"(1) For those unoccupied lands in which the public have rights and which therefore cannot be leased, e.g., roads, halots, drinking water tanks, embankments, wells, etc.

(2) for plots available for settlement whether for cultivation or occupation or sairats;

(3) for purchased, resumed or abandoned holdings and;

(4) for diluviated khas land.

16. From the above rule, it appears that water tanks used by public cannot be leased out. In the case in hand, we find that in violation of the above rule, the land of plot No. 794 was leased out to the plaintiff. It is, however, contended that in the remarks column of C.S. record through mistake it was written “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয”. In this connection, it is important to note here that according to section 103 B (5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act, every entry made in a record-of-rights shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved by evidence to be incorrect. The plaintiff, how-ever, could not rebut the presumption of correctness of the entry made in the C.S. khatian including the entry made in its remarks column in which it was written “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয”.

17. Over and above, the suit land was locally investigated by an Advocate Commissioner who submitted a report stating as follows:

"There is water in suit plot No. 794. The area of the watery portion is .21 decimals. Depth of water is 2 to 21/2 cubits from the edge of the water towards the middle of the watery portion. There is not a drop of water in suit plot No. 2546/2583."

18. Therefore, it appears that plot No. 794 is not a derelict tank. The plaintiff, however, managed to obtain a report that the tank of suit plot No. 794 is derelict. As for Plot 2546/2583, it appears that there was not a drop of water in it when the commission was held on March 25, 1985, that is, during the lean session. But in his report the Advocate Commissioner, however, shows as follows:

"The suit plot No. 2546/2583 is bounded by River Bhadai on the north, west and south by the land of Mouza Baronjal on the east"

The Advocate Commission also found:

"As to plot No. 2583 (though it should be plot No. 2546/2583), it is a dry fallow land in dry time and during rainy session it turns into a river."

<u>19. I do not find any rationale why the land of suit plot No. 2546/2583 bounded by river on three sides was leased out to the plaintiff. For the uninterrupted flow of the river during the rainy season, such types of land should not be leased out to anybody. In-discriminate leasing out of such land owned by the Government not only impede the normal flow of the river but also creates environmental hazards.</u>

<u>20. Both the Court below found faults with the officials of the Government in leasing out the suit land to the plaintiff. The lease would not have come into being, had the plaintiff not colluded with the officials of the Government. Therefore, he who commits wrong cannot take advantage of his wrong. Since the Government is of the people, the land owned by the Government, in fact, belongs to the people. The Government is a mere manager of such land. Government will come and go but the land belonging to the people will remain forever. For the illegal actions of some Government officials, the people cannot be deprived of their right over such land. If any irregularity is detected in leasing out any land standing in the name of the Government, such land must be restored to its original position before taking any punitive action against the unscrupulous Government officials.</u>

21. In the facts and circumstances, it appears that the land of suit plot Nos. 794 and 2546/2583 should not have been leased out to anybody.

22. In this connection reliance may be made on the case of Jafar Ali Vs. Khagendra Chandra Dutta and Others 1983 BLD 32 in which M.H. Rahman, J observed as follows:

In the present case the land was recorded in the C.S. record as well as S.A. Khatian as “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয”. As the public had rights in the disputed land, the settlement made in favour of the plaintiff was not legally done, and by the impugned orders such settlement was correctly cancelled by the revenue authorities."

23. The trial Court relied upon the case of Abdul Majid and Others Vs. the Province of East Pakistan and-Others (1971) 23 DLR 203. In that case, settlement of khas land was made to the plaintiff on the recommendation of the Deputy Collector, Revenue and on the approval of the Joint Collector (Revenue). Thereupon the plaintiffs were inducted on the lands but on defendant's representation, the Commissioner cancelled the settlement. Question raised was whether or not the Commissioner in the absence of any appellate power could cancel settlement by exercising his general supervisory power. It was held that the Commissioner had no jurisdiction to set aside the settlement made by the Collector in favour of the plaintiffs, by exercising his general supervisory power specially in a case where such cancellation would affect the right of a third party citizen of the State.

24. In the case referred to above the lease was cancelled by the Divisional Commissioner. In the case in hand, the lease was cancelled by the Additional Deputy Commissioner who is also the Deputy Collector of the District. Admittedly, the lease was granted by the then Sub-Divisional Officer who was under the direct control of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) and Additional Deputy Collector. As soon as the fraud was detected in taking lease of the suit land, the Additional Deputy Commissioner and Additional Deputy Collector had to cancel the lease. In the case of Jafar Ali Vs. Khagendra Chandra Dutta, 1983 BLD 32 referred to earlier, the lease granted by the S.D.O. in favour the plaintiff was cancelled by the Additional Deputy Commissioner and M.H. Rahman J found cancellation of the lease valid. There-fore, the case reported in 23 DLR at page 203 relied upon by the learned Subordinate Judge has no manner of application on the facts and in circumstances of the instant case.

25. In the light of the findings made before, the lands of suit plot Nos. 794 and 2546/2583 should not have been leased out at all.

26. In the result, the Rule is made absolute and judgment and decree dated 21.4.1990 passed by the learned Additional District Judge affirming judgment and decree dated 21.12.1983 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge are hereby set aside and the suit is dis-missed.

27. The Government is directed not to lease out the land of suit plot Nos. 794 and 2546/2583 to anybody.

28. No order as to costs.

29. Send down the L.C. record with a copy of the judgment.

End.
